blocks.raw: # Limits and Errors
blocks.text: Limits and Errors

blocks.raw: ## Idempotent Requests
blocks.text: Idempotent Requests

blocks.raw: The API supports idempotency for safely retrying non-idempotent requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. This is typically used where you are unsure of the status of the request. For example, if a POST request to create a payment fails due to a network connection error you can retry the request with the same x-mod-nonce to guarantee that only a single payment is created.
blocks.text: The API supports idempotency for safely retrying non-idempotent requests without accidentally performing the same operation twice. This is typically used where you are unsure of the status of the request. For example, if a POST request to create a payment fails due to a network connection error you can retry the request with the same x-mod-nonce to guarantee that only a single payment is created.

blocks.raw: To retry a POST request idempotently you can:
blocks.text: To retry a POST request idempotently you can:

blocks.raw:
* Reuse the same x-mod-nonce as the original POST request and
* Set the header` x-mod-retry = true`
blocks.text: Reuse the same x-mod-nonce as the original POST request andSet the header x-mod-retry = true

blocks.raw:
This will send back the same response for requests made with the same `x-mod-nonce` for 48 hours. Do not retry after 48 hours as the request could be executed as a new request after this.\
Do not use the same nonce for GET requests as this will just return an error. You also cannot use the same nonce with different request parameters.\
If you wish to resend a payment request because a previous one has failed, e.g. the account did not have enough balance at the time, then you will need to use a new nonce. Please refer to [Error handling](https://modulr.readme.io/docs/error-handling) .

blocks.raw: ## Rate Limiting & Quotas
blocks.text: Rate Limiting & Quotas

blocks.raw: In order to protect all system clients from the actions of a single client limits are placed on how many requests can be made in a short period (rate limit) and over a longer period (quota)
blocks.text: In order to protect all system clients from the actions of a single client limits are placed on how many requests can be made in a short period (rate limit) and over a longer period (quota)

blocks.raw: You should not experience these errors in the course of normal operations for the vast majority of clients. If you do please look into the volume/pattern of requests you are making and check for any issues. Note: Limits and quotas work across all your requests
blocks.text: You should not experience these errors in the course of normal operations for the vast majority of clients. If you do please look into the volume/pattern of requests you are making and check for any issues. Note: Limits and quotas work across all your requests

blocks.raw: All endpoints are rate limited (X requests in X seconds), and each API key has a quota. These are to protect the service from a particular user's unusual activity.
blocks.text: All endpoints are rate limited (X requests in X seconds), and each API key has a quota. These are to protect the service from a particular user's unusual activity.

blocks.raw: Our standard rate profile is:
blocks.text: Our standard rate profile is:

blocks.raw:
Number of Requests Period of Time
8000 10 minutes

blocks.raw: ## Backwards compatibility
blocks.text: Backwards compatibility

blocks.raw: The following api changes are considered backwards compatible, and should be handled by you:
blocks.text: The following api changes are considered backwards compatible, and should be handled by you:

blocks.raw:
* Adding new API endpoints
* Adding new properties to the responses from existing API endpoints
* Reordering properties returned from existing API endpoints
* Adding optional request parameters to existing API endpoints
* Altering the format or length of IDs
* Altering the `message` attributes returned by validation failures / other errors
* Sending webhooks for new event types

blocks.raw: ## MIME Types
blocks.text: MIME Types

blocks.raw: All requests and responses are JSON-formatted. You must pass the standard JSON MIME type (application/json). Other content types will return a `500 error – “Content type not supported”`
blocks.text: All requests and responses are JSON-formatted. You must pass the standard JSON MIME type (application/json). Other content types will return a 500 error – “Content type not supported”

blocks.raw: ## Response Status Codes
blocks.text: Response Status Codes

blocks.raw: The API uses the following response status codes:
blocks.text: The API uses the following response status codes:

blocks.raw:
| Code | Description                                                                                                                |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 200  | OK - The request has succeeded. The client can read the result of the request in the body and the headers of the response. |
| 201  | Created - The resource was created successfully. The response may have information about the newly created resource.       |
| 400  | Bad Request - This is likely caused by validation errors, response body will provide further information.                  |
| 403  | Forbidden - The client is not allowed to access the resource                                                               |
| 404  | Not Found - The requested resource doesn’t exist. Please check documentation and the request.                              |
| 405  | Method Not Allowed - HTTP method used to access this resource is incorrect, please check documentation                     |
| 500  | Internal Server Error - Response body may contain further information                                                      |

blocks.raw: ## Error detail
blocks.text: Error detail

blocks.raw: Errors on the Modulr API will return a 4XX or a 5XX HTTP response code. Additional information about the error will be returned in the response body, in the format:
blocks.text: Errors on the Modulr API will return a 4XX or a 5XX HTTP response code. Additional information about the error will be returned in the response body, in the format:

blocks.raw:
```
{
"field": "id",
"code": "NOTFOUND",
"message": "Customer not found for id: C0200002"
}
```
## Pagination
blocks.text: Pagination

blocks.raw: Responses for list endpoints (Accounts, Transactions, Beneficiaries) are paginated by default.
blocks.text: Responses for list endpoints (Accounts, Transactions, Beneficiaries) are paginated by default.

blocks.raw: ### Request
blocks.text: Request

blocks.raw: The following options are available on all cursor-paginated endpoints:
blocks.text: The following options are available on all cursor-paginated endpoints:

blocks.raw:
* Page - Page to fetch (0-indexed)
* Size - number of elements to return. Maximum value is 500
blocks.text: Page - Page to fetch (0-indexed)Size - number of elements to return. Maximum value is 500

blocks.raw: ### Response
blocks.text: Response

blocks.raw: Paginated results are always returned in an array, and include the following meta data:
blocks.text: Paginated results are always returned in an array, and include the following meta data:

blocks.raw:
```

"size": 15,
"totalSize": 189,
"page": 1,
"totalPages": 13
}
```

## Time zones
blocks.text: Time zones

blocks.raw: All timestamps are formatted as ISO8601 with timezone information. For API calls that allow for a timestamp to be specified, we use that exact timestamp. These timestamps look something like `2016-06-01T12:00:00.111Z`. All times should be sent in UTC time zone.

blocks.raw: For endpoints that require dates, we expect a date string of the format `YYYY-MM-DD`, where an example would look like `2016-06-01`.
